what_this_proves: The automated path-aware critique reaches two providers on this seat. Two live runs, both --dry-run on purpose: the artifact itself is gated at the SET-TERMINAL close, which is now Session 8.

runs.label: A. config default pin
runs.proves: the SERVANT-GUARD fix. The default openai pin is gpt-5.4, already a served model id, so the alias defect never applied to it -- this is the arm that raised DeterministicServantViolation in Session 4, and it now returns a schema-valid verdict.
runs.ledger_note: this run predates the accounting fix landing, so it wrote no router-metrics row. Its cost is therefore UNMEASURED, not zero.

runs.label: B. pinned to the alias that returned HTTP 400
runs.proves: the ALIAS fix end-to-end, with the exact pin that returned HTTP 400 model_not_found twice in Session 4. The ledger row records the SERVED id gpt-5.6-sol, not the alias that was sent before.
runs.also_proves: the ACCOUNTING fix. Set 113 S4's three critique runs wrote no ledger row at all; these two rows are the first critique spend this repo has ever measured. And the cost ceiling binds again: the openai arm's $1.3294 against cost_ceiling_usd 1.00 is the documented one-final-forced-verdict allowance, whereas before the alias fix _pricing_for read $0.00 for an alias and the ceiling could not bind at all.
